target_moa.text: Ipilimumab is a fully human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that blocks cytotoxic T-lymphocyte antigen 4 (CTLA-4, CD152); by blocking the binding of CTLA-4 to the B7 molecules (CD80/CD86) on antigen-presenting cells it potentiates T-cell activation and the anti-tumor immune response.

citations.quote: Ipilimumab is a fully human monoclonal immunoglobulin (IgG1k) specific for human cytotoxic T lymphocyte antigen 4 (CTLA-4, CD152), which is expressed on a subset of activated T cells. Ipilimumab is produced by recombinant DNA technology in a Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) mammalian cell expression system.

The proposed mechanism of action for ipilimumab is interference with the interaction of CTLA-4 (cytotoxic T lymphocyte antigen 4; CD152) with the B7 molecules (CD80/CD86) on antigen-presenting cells. This results in subsequent blockade of the inhibitory modulation of T cell activation and potentiation of the immune response.

Ipilimumab is a fully human monoclonal immunoglobulin (IgG1k) specific for human cytotoxic T lymphocyte antigen 4 (CTLA-4, CD152), which is expressed on a subset of activated T cells. Ipilimumab is produced by recombinant DNA technology in a Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) mammalian cell expression system.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=5%) are fatigue, diarrhea, pruritus, rash, and colitis. In Study 1 (3 mg/kg arm): diarrhea 32% (Grade 3-5 5%), colitis 8% (Grade 3-5 5%), pruritus 31%, rash 29%. The major risks are severe and fatal immune-mediated adverse reactions, including immune-mediated enterocolitis (Grade 3-5 in 7%), hepatitis, dermatitis, neuropathy, and endocrinopathy (Grade 3-4 in 1.8%).
